findings.title: Routine cleanup operations logged at Error level with nil errors
findings.body: The new cleanup code logs every routine operation at Error level: r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, "cond", cond, "err", err) and r.log.Error("cleaned annotations by time", "count", len(ids), "affected", x, "err", y). Cleanup runs as a background job that should never be considered an error; previously this code did not log at all. The "err" field is always nil at these sites (errors are returned early), so the messages convey no actionable signal but will spam the error log on every cycle, making real errors harder to find and tripping error-rate alerts in monitoring. The level should be Info or Debug, and the meaningless "err" field should be removed.

findings.title: Full annotation IDs and full WHERE condition dumped into logs on every batch
findings.body: Each batch emits "ids", ids (the entire int64 slice) and the raw SQL condition into the log. With AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize set in the tens of thousands (the new test case uses 32767), this produces extremely verbose log entries on every cycle. Logging thousands of integers is not useful and increases log volume/cost; an only the count and a truncated identifier (or none) should be logged.

findings.title: Cleanup ticker frequency silently changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The diff changes the cleanup ticker from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`, a 10x increase in how often the entire cleanup job (including annotation cleanup, expired snapshots, dashboard versions, images, user invites, short URLs and query history) runs. This change is not mentioned in the PR description and is unrelated to the deadlock fix. It will significantly increase database query load and log volume (especially given the new Error-level logging above) on every Grafana instance. Either it should be reverted, made configurable, or at minimum called out in the PR description / release notes.

findings.title: Annotation cleanup tests now skipped under -short
findings.body: The tests `TestAnnotationCleanUp` and `TestOldAnnotationsAreDeletedFirst` have been renamed to `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp` and `TestIntegrationOldAnnotationsAreDeletedFirst` and now call `t.Skip` when `testing.Short()` is true. Previously these tests always ran. Any developer or CI step that runs `go test -short ./pkg/services/annotations/...` will lose coverage of the new split-statement cleanup logic (including the SQLite 32767-batch path that was added). If the intent is to keep this as a required test, the skip should be removed or the package should ensure integration tests are always run in CI.

findings.title: O(n^2) string concatenation when inlining IDs into SQLite DELETE
findings.body: In `deleteByIDs`, when SQLite is used with a batch size greater than 999 the IDs are concatenated into a single SQL string via repeated `fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`. This is O(n^2) in the number of IDs and, with the new default-style batch size of 32767 (and tests using batch sizes in that range), produces hundreds of thousands of intermediate string allocations per batch. Using `strings.Builder` (or `strings.Join` after pre-formatting) would be linear and cheaper.

findings.title: Stale/incorrect "condition must be supplied" error message
findings.body: `fetchIDs` checks `if condition == ""` and returns `fmt.Errorf("condition must be supplied; cannot fetch IDs from entire table")`, but `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` passes a non-empty condition that begins with `NOT EXISTS (...)` followed directly by the LIMIT clause with no `WHERE` keyword. The error message implies a missing WHERE clause would result in a full-table SELECT, but the guard will still fire whenever any caller forgets to prepend a WHERE. This is a minor wording/logic mismatch and could mask a real bug in future callers; the message should describe the actual invariant (e.g., "condition cannot be empty") or be removed in favor of a real precondition.
